questions: How many NbSe2/CrBr3 devices did you fabricate and measure, and how many showed the field-free diode effect and the inverted sign-change fields (Bcf < 0, Bcb > 0)?
Why were the others set aside?
Which ranges of field (sweep amplitude and step), temperature and bias current did you measure beyond the ones shown, for example beyond the ±50 mT sweeps at 200 mK in Fig. 2?
What does the second-best device or dataset look like? Device #2 is in the SM; for device #3 in Fig. 3(a), what are |Ic+| and |Ic−| at zero field, and how was the 705 µA bias chosen?

What is the remanent field of your magnet at nominal zero after the ±50 mT sweeps and after the ±6 T training, and how did you measure it? Since η goes from 45.3% at about −10 mT to −35.7% at 0 mT, an offset of a few mT would matter.

If you train device #1, then warm it at zero field above the NbSe2 transition but below the CrBr3 ordering temperature and cool again, does the −35.7% survive, or does η return toward the −15.2% you see after zero-field cooling?

Have you measured a bare NbSe2 flake, an uncovered part of the same flake, or a NbSe2/hBN/CrBr3 stack through the same field history, and could the self-field, Meissner and geometric-asymmetry controls from the SM appear in the main text?

What are the NbSe2 and CrBr3 thicknesses (layer numbers) in each device, and how do you extract Ic from the dV/dI peaks (lock-in or numerical derivative, current step); could you share the raw V(I) data behind Figs. 1(d) and 2(c)?
